Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-01
Start time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Maya Rodriguez (CEO), Ethan Clarke (CTO), Priya Nair (VP Eng), Liam O'Connor (VP Product), Avery Chen (Head of Sales), Zara Ahmed (Head of Infra), many others (all-hands)

Maya: Quick state of company, focus on reliability and cost, shoutouts to infra team, mention of SOC2 work, hiring push for infra and customer reliability.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: alright good morning everyone thanks for joining our march all-hands, um I think we can get started, we've got a lot to cover, we'll keep it tight but also leave time for q and a at the end.
[00:22] Ethan: hi team, quick note on infra, first shout out to zara and the infra crew for the Dedicated autoscaler POC we ran last week, the results are promising but there's some tail latency we want to shave. (inaudible) the KV cache behavior under burst is still the biggest knob.
[00:45] Zara: yeah just to add, the autoscaler reduces idle GPU time by about 28% in the test, we still saw a couple of 95th pct spikes when sequence lengths jumped - looks like batching heuristics need a tiny bit of tuning. we'll post the raw bench spreadsheet in the infra channel.
[01:15] Priya: engineering's focus next two sprints is: (a) prioritize the batching heuristics work, (b) improve the KV cache eviction policy to avoid cold-starts, and (c) ship the first internal beta of the autoscaler. hope to have beta next 3 weeks.
[01:42] Lily (PM-muted): question from product folks — how does this interact with per-route caching and our existing prefix cache?
[01:55] Rohit: quick answer, autoscaler works at infra level, prefix/KV cache is orthogonal but we are adding hooks so the autoscaler can prefer nodes with warm KV cache for pinned customers. still early but that's the plan.
[02:20] Maya: on the business side, we closed a couple of meaningful deals in february that show demand for dedicated capacity from mid-market. big props to avery and the sales team. avery, can you 2 mins on pipeline?
[02:35] Avery: yeah thanks. we've seen an uptick in RFPs from fintech and healthcare. biggest asks: VPC/on-prem options, SOC2 evidence, and predictable latency SLAs. we're positioning Dedicated + Private as the go-to for those deals — sales playbook is in progress. i'll share a draft by next week.
[03:02] Alyssa (fake): question: any movement on pricing for reserved capacity?
[03:10] Avery: pricing is still in review with ops and finance, but expect a more formal tiered commit model: monthly/annual with burst credits — details soon.
[03:25] Liam: product update quick hit — Optimize is getting a new quantization recommender and a batching analyzer in the console, should help customers reduce unit cost without manual tuning. also we're adding a per-route cost breakdown into the console UI.
[03:55] Audience murmur / crosstalk
[04:10] Ethan: quick tech note — we've made changes to the kernel selector that cut median token latency by ~8% on our latest test models, though as zara said there's a 95th pct regressed for some configs. investigating.
[04:35] Maya: ok good, security update, nina?
[04:42] Nina: security — SOC2 readiness: internal controls mostly in place, vendor assessments almost done, external audit scheduled for late q2. timeline feels realistic but we should prepare for a couple of remediation items. security will publish a status doc by 2026-03-08.
[05:05] Maya: that one is important for a lot of our enterprise deals so please prioritize.
[05:12] Zeke (someone off mike): are we still planning private on-prem for that healthcare customer?
[05:20] Maya: yes, engineering and security are aligned, we need a runbook for air-gapped deploys — zara can you take point?
[05:29] Zara: yep we'll create a runbook and add it to the private deployments checklist.
[05:40] [06:00] Hiring / People update
[06:05] Maya: hiring — headcount approval for Q2 came through, priority hires: infra SRE (3), runtime engineers (4), security engineer (1), and solutions engineers (2). we are focusing on speed for infra and runtime. hiring panel details will be posted.
[06:30] Priya: we're also reworking the interview loop for runtime candidates to include a short perf debugging task, keeps things practical.
[06:45] Maya: ok finances — high level, burn is in line with plan, runway unchanged, revenue growing month-over-month but we need to accelerate large deals for enterprise traction. finance will share month-end numbers in the #finance channel.
[07:05] [07:30] Product roadmap section
[07:33] Liam: roadmap highlights: 1) Dedicated autoscaler beta (internal) 2) Optimize toolkit improvements (quantization advisor, batching analyzer) 3) Private deployment runbook & hardened packaging 4) Console per-route cost breakdown 5) Eval / regression monitoring for prompt sets. target dates in deck.
[08:05] Audience question: how soon can customers get the autoscaler in beta?
[08:12] Priya: internal beta in 3 weeks, external pilot in 6 weeks assuming nothing major shows up in the internal run.
[08:30] [09:00] Sales win callout
[09:05] Avery: one customer signed annual committed capacity, expected ARR impact modest but it's a big validation for the Dedicated motion. will disclose details in the sales update.
[09:25] [10:00] Q&A — mixed questions on latency, cost, SOC2, and private deploys
[10:05] Employee question: will we have better docs for on-prem?
[10:12] Zara: yes docs are a priority, will include network diagrams and step-by-step packaging.
[10:22] Employee followup: any change to free tier or credits for pilots?
[10:27] Avery: no change right now, we want to keep credits for quick evaluation but will gate bigger pilots behind a pilot contract for cost and support reasons.
[10:40] [12:00] Tech deep dive snippet
[12:05] Ethan: for those interested in the kernel selector, we'll host a tech deep dive next tuesday — it's an open invite to eng and infra folks, we'll share notes and the bench spreadsheet in the tech channel.
[12:30] [13:00] Cross-talk, small interruptions, laughter
[13:22] Maya: quick recognition — shout out to infra on the autoscaler POC and to the data team for the new benchmarking harness. big thanks.
[13:40] [14:00] Closing remarks and explicit next steps
[14:05] Maya: ok quick recap: engineering to post autoscaler beta timeline, security publish SOC2 status doc by 3/8, sales to share Dedicated playbook draft next week, hiring to post interview loops and reqs. we'll publish slides and recording tomorrow. any last Qs?
[14:35] Audience: thanks!
[14:40] Maya: thanks everyone, have a great rest of your week.
[14:50] Meeting end
